narrative.overview:
A logistics manifest is functional, precise, and trustworthy. Every item has its place. No decorative flourishes, no ornament — just clear information in a deliberate hierarchy. The interface earns trust through clarity and speed, not visual appeal.

The system treats red as signal, not decoration. #e63329 appears only where action is demanded. Against the warm neutral ground (#f0eeeb), the red doesn't shout — it directs.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default: depth through tonal layering, not shadows
Red as a functional signal, not an accent for its own sake
Two-typeface system: ABC Normal for display/headings, Inter for body
Generous whitespace around information blocks; tight spacing inside them
No decorative borders, no gradient text, no glass effects

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Red is used on less than 10% of any given screen. It appears on interactive elements only — never on backgrounds, dividers, or decorative accents. If red occupies more than one element per viewport tier, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Manifest Rule
rules.body: Every heading earns its place. If a heading can be removed without losing information, remove it. The typography hierarchy is a cargo list, not a table of contents.

dos: Do use Signal Red for exactly one interactive element per viewport tier.
Do separate surfaces through background color, never shadows.
Do keep body text at Muted Ink (#5a5a5a) or darker. No light gray text on white.
Do use the two-typeface system: ABC Normal for display/headings, Inter for everything else.
Do let white space replace decorative elements.
donts: Don't use red for backgrounds, dividers, or decorative accents.
Don't use gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
Don't use glassmorphism, blurred backdrops, or frosted effects.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left/right > 1px as accent).
Don't use bounce or elastic easing.
Don't use marketing buzzwords in UI text.
Don't use tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section.
Don't ship motion that has no prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
